description: Hey everyone! 👋 I’m a Computer Science student interested in AI, Data Science, ML, and Python. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I’m excited to work on Dancing with the SARs 🛰️🌍 and explore NISAR radar data. Looking for teammates interested in AI/ML, remote sensing, GIS, visualization, or UI/UX. Let’s build something awesome together! 🚀
summary:
Earth Rhythm AI is an interactive web observatory that turns complex NASA–ISRO NISAR radar data into understandable stories about Earth’s changing surface. We developed a scientific processing pipeline and a web application using ten satellite acquisitions over Egypt’s Fayoum Oasis. Animated maps, before-and-after comparisons, time-series charts, six guided story chapters, and an AI guide help users explore seasonal crop growth, harvest patterns, and changes in water and land surfaces. The platform also includes exploratory shoreline-inundation scenarios and explainable next-pass forecasts.

Our project addresses the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge by showing how different radar polarizations reveal vegetation structure and surface conditions, while making these insights accessible to non-specialists. Every layer retains its source and metadata, and the interface clearly separates observations, detected changes, and interpretations.

Earth Rhythm AI matters because understanding agricultural and water-system changes can support better resource management in water-scarce regions. It connects satellite science with local concerns while making uncertainty and limitations visible.

PROJECT DETAILS — EARTH RHYTHM

Listening to the Nile's 120-Day Pulse with NASA-ISRO L-Band Radar

Earth Rhythm is an interactive radar-science observatory and guided story experience built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("Dancing with the SARs"). Over 10 consecutive 12-day satellite passes (June 23 – October 21, 2026), it turns raw NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) microwave echoes over Egypt's Fayoum Oasis into a living story—helping anyone see how crops grow, how farmers irrigate dry soil, how wind ripples desert lakes, and how shorelines shift before the next flood arrives.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"Earth Rhythm Observatory — Chapter 1 Physical Scattering Map and Story Mode" ]

Earth Rhythm Observatory — Chapter 1 Physical Scattering Map and Story Mode

How Does Our Solution Work?

Every 12 days, NISAR flies over Fayoum Oasis (Track 129 / Frame 016, 4,912 km²) and beams 24 cm L-band radio waves down through clouds, dust, and upper leaves. Unlike normal optical satellites that only photograph green leaf color, 24 cm waves penetrate deep into plant stems and wet soil—listening back in two "orientations" (polarizations) at once:

  • HV (Cross-Polarization — The Plant Volume Detector): Horizontally transmitted waves bounce around inside 3D tangles of stems and leaves, twisting back vertically. More canopy volume = brighter HV.
  • HH (Co-Polarization — The Soil Moisture, Plowing & Water Detector): Horizontally transmitted waves bounce straight back off wet soil, plowed furrows, city walls, and wind-rippled water.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"Mermaid diagram" ]

Instead of drowning visitors in raw radar noise, Earth Rhythm guides you through Fayoum's 120-day rhythm in six interactive chapters, assisted by Echo (our built-in AI science companion):

  • Chapter 1 — The Desert & The Oasis in Four True Radar Colors: Right outside the 1,934 km² green agricultural oasis lies the hyper-arid Western Desert. Independent NASA POWER weather records show just 0.15 mm of total rain across 133 days (0.00 mm on all 10 satellite passes), proving every drop powering this oasis arrives via the Bahr Youssef Nile canal. Our decoupled color map separates Lush Green (HV crop canopies), Vivid Red (HH urban buildings), Deep Blue to Cyan (calm water to wind ripples), and Warm Sand (bare soil and limestone desert).
  • Chapter 2 — The Summer Growth Wave (June 23 → August 10): Using our Split-Screen Swipe Slider, you watch 763.88 km² (39.5%) of farmland ignite in HV brightness as summer maize, sorghum, and cotton thicken. At our eastern oasis checkpoint (Sennuris / Tamia), HV climbs +10.77 dB, tracking independent Sentinel-2 optical greenness (NDVI) with a strong correlation of r=0.93r = 0.93r=0.93.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"Split-Screen Swipe Comparison and Linear-Power Calibration Tables" ]

Split-Screen Swipe Comparison and Linear-Power Calibration Tables

  • Chapter 3 — Harvest Meets Autumn Emergence (August 10 → October 21): Basin-wide averages barely budge (2.05 dB), hiding an intense seasonal handoff: 594.83 km² of summer crops are harvested (-HV) right next to 174.17 km² of newly planted autumn fields (+HV) rising steadily across eight straight passes (+11.54 dB). Even better, when tiny winter seedlings sprout in late October, optical NDVI rebounds to 0.661 while 24 cm radar HV stays quiet (-19.89 dB)—because thin blades are smaller than the wavelength (Rayleigh-transparent) until woody stems develop.
  • Chapter 4 — The Plot Twist: When HH and HV Disagree: Across 440.7 km² of farmland, HH and HV tell completely different stories. At our southeastern farmland spot, HV drops -2.60 dB after harvest while HH jumps +8.24 dB from deep chisel plowing and immediate flood irrigation. A single-channel radar would mistake that wet bare dirt for sudden crop growth; dual-polarization catches both events in our 7-Class Regime Map. Meanwhile, southern drainage basins swing 12.35 dB in HH as smooth mirror-like standing water drains into rough wet mudflats.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"What Changed Map, 10-Date Time Series Chart, Sentinel-2 Cross-Check, and Rain-Free Weather Strip" ]

What Changed Map, 10-Date Time Series Chart, Sentinel-2 Cross-Check, and Rain-Free Weather Strip

  • Chapter 5 — Wind Ripples on Lake Qarun & Rescuing El-Qarn Island: Over Lake Qarun, HV stays pinned near the sensor noise floor (~ -24.9 dB), while HH swings by 11.17 dB whenever 2–5 m/s winds stir tiny capillary Bragg waves across the water. By combining 10 backscatter passes with 9 interferometric coherence pairs (γ\gammaγ) and wind-variability checks, Earth Rhythm maps 310.18 km² of pure open water (IoU = 0.9243, 99.19% precision against NASA's optical OPERA DSWx-HLS water benchmark) without erasing +43 m-tall El-Qarn Island (99.2% preserved).

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"Overview Basin Dashboard Showing Seasonal Growth vs. Harvest Balance" ]

Overview Basin Dashboard Showing Seasonal Growth vs. Harvest Balance

  • Chapter 6 — Honest Noise Rulers & The 12-Day Forecast (November 2, 2026): Before trusting any pixel change, we measure 218,705 unchanging limestone desert pixels (349.93 km²) as a natural calibration ruler and filter speckles strictly in physical power before converting to decibels. We also inspect exploratory 12-day interferograms (L2_GUNW)—and honestly refuse to claim ground sinking because natural atmospheric water-vapor ramps (8.80–18.78 mm) outweigh 12-day ground compaction (< 0.5 mm). Finally, our Explainable Forecaster projects next-pass (November 2) flood risk, crop regimes, and drainage surge impacts across Lake Qarun's closed basin.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"Explainable Flood Risk Forecast Map and Drainage Surge Simulator" ]

Explainable Flood Risk Forecast Map and Drainage Surge Simulator

The Math Behind the Scenes (Light & Honest)

  • Energy-Conserving Speckle Smoothing: Radar echoes contain salt-and-pepper speckle. Converting pixels to decibels before averaging computes a geometric mean instead of an arithmetic mean (log⁡10P‾<log⁡10Pˉ\overline{\log_{10} P} < \log_{10} \bar{P}log10​P​<log10​Pˉ, Jensen's inequality), creating a fake -0.5 to -2.5 dB dark bias. We aggregate 10 m pixels 4×4 to 40 m and apply a 3×3 Adaptive Lee filter strictly in linear power (γ0\gamma^0γ0, m2/m2\text{m}^2/\text{m}^2m2/m2)—boosting the Equivalent Number of Looks (ENL=μ2/σ2\text{ENL} = \mu^2 / \sigma^2ENL=μ2/σ2) from 4.9 to 153–481 while preserving true mean power within 0.08%—before converting to decibels: γdB0=10log⁡10(γ0),ΔdB=10log⁡10 ⁣(PafterPbefore)\gamma^0_{\text{dB}} = 10 \log_{10}(\gamma^0), \qquad \Delta\text{dB} = 10 \log_{10}\!\left(\frac{P_{\text{after}}}{P_{\text{before}}}\right)γdB0​=10log10​(γ0),ΔdB=10log10​(Pbefore​Pafter​​)
  • Desert-Locked Change Thresholds: Over 1.97 million stable desert pixel-pairs, we set each channel's change cutoff τ\tauτ as the conservative maximum of theoretical speckle noise (3σspeckle3\sigma_{\text{speckle}}3σspeckle​), robust desert spread (3σMAD3\sigma_{\text{MAD}}3σMAD​), and the empirical 99th percentile (P99P_{99}P99​): τHH=2.73 dB,τHV=2.03 dB\tau_{\text{HH}} = 2.73\text{ dB}, \qquad \tau_{\text{HV}} = 2.03\text{ dB}τHH​=2.73 dB,τHV​=2.03 dB Any smaller shift is treated as background noise rather than surface change.
  • Exploratory Interferometry Guard: Unwrapped radar phase (Δϕ\Delta\phiΔϕ) converts to apparent line-of-sight range via ΔdLOS=−λ4πΔϕ\Delta d_{\text{LOS}} = -\frac{\lambda}{4\pi}\Delta\phiΔdLOS​=−4πλ​Δϕ (λ≈24 cm\lambda \approx 24\text{ cm}λ≈24 cm), strictly masking out unstable targets with coherence γ<0.50\gamma < 0.50γ<0.50.
  • Explainable Flood & Next-Pass Forecasting: Four transparent physical signals—HH dielectric water index (38%), 12-day phase instability 1−γ1-\gamma1−γ (24%), 3-pass wetting velocity (22%), and NISAR_DEM shoreline proximity (16%)—combine with a damped trend backscatter model. Hid Pass 10 (Oct 21) and predicted it strictly from Passes 1–9: ROC-AUC = 0.9998 (full basin) / 0.9976 (1.5 km shoreline), shoreline IoU = 0.8871, HH RMSE = 1.03 dB, and HV RMSE = 0.95 dB, feeding a hydraulically connected Height Above Nearest Drainage (HAND) surge simulator (15,434 ha baseline to 24,815 ha at +1.0 m).

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Unmasks Hidden Agricultural Signals: Separates true crop biomass growth from bare-soil flood irrigation (440.7 km² of divergence) where optical cameras or single-channel radar mislead.
  • Works in Any Weather & Lighting: 24 cm radar penetrates clouds, dust, and upper leaves on a guaranteed 12-day cadence.
  • Speaks Human & Scientist Fluently: Plain-language summaries, interactive dashboards, a 3-minute reading guide, and Echo AI help students and policymakers understand every map—while GIS experts can inspect exact dB ribbons, 11 provenance fields, and download calibrated Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs.
  • Lightweight on Bandwidth & Hardware: Selective cloud range-streaming trims 657+ GB of satellite scenes down to 455 MB locally (99.93% reduction) with zero loss of native calibration.
  • Honest by Design: Every finding separates what was Observed, what Changed above noise, and what is an Interpretation (hypothesis)—never disguising weather noise or assumptions as certainty.

What Is the Intended Impact?

Because Bahr Youssef Nile canal water drives 100% of Fayoum's irrigation (0.15 mm total summer rainfall), Earth Rhythm turns NISAR's 12-day cadence into a practical blueprint for arid river basins worldwide:

  1. Canal-Scale Irrigation Auditing: Spotting bare-soil wetting and flood ponding across irrigation districts so water ministries can catch tail-end canal shortages early.
  2. All-Weather Crop & Phenology Monitoring: Pairing L-band stem structure (HV) with optical leaf greenness (NDVI) to track staggered planting and harvesting across millions of smallholder plots.
  3. Closed-Basin Lake & Shoreline Early Warning: Tracking Lake Qarun and Wadi El Rayan margins (165.85 km² dynamic zone) and quantifying cropland (313–659 ha) and road corridors exposed during drainage surges.
  4. Preventing Radar Misinterpretation: Teaching communities and analysts why single-pair InSAR phase ramps are mostly atmospheric moisture rather than sinking land until 20–30+ passes accumulate.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Coding Languages: Python (scientific radar processing, statistical analysis, and data serving) and TypeScript / HTML / CSS (interactive browser observatory).
  • Scientific & Mapping Software: NASA Earthdata / ASF discovery tools, HDF5 multidimensional cube tools, GDAL / PROJ geospatial raster & Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF tooling, NumPy & SciPy vectorized math, React & MapLibre GL JS dual-canvas interactive web mapping, and hand-crafted SVG charts.
  • Datasets & AI Companions: NASA-ISRO NISAR (L2_GCOV & L2_GUNW), NASA OPERA DSWx-HLS, NISAR_WATERMASK & NISAR_DEM, NASA POWER daily weather, ESA Sentinel-2 L2A optical NDVI, and multi-provider Echo AI support (Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Mistral, and local Ollama).
  • Deployment & QA: Docker containerization, Hugging Face Spaces serverless static hosting, automated scientific invariant verification (11 physical & metadata checks), and manual end-to-end UI verification.
  • Hardware: Engineered deliberately to run on a standard consumer workstation / laptop (verified on a 64-bit Windows 11, 12-core Intel CPU machine with no GPU or compute cluster required), made possible by selective cloud range-streaming.

How Is Our Project Creative?

  • Streaming the Needle, Not the Haystack: Reading internal satellite chunk maps over HTTPS shrinks 657+ GB down to 455 MB so everyday laptops can work directly with NASA's flagship L-band data.
  • Turning the Sahara into a Calibration Lab: Instead of guessing a change cutoff, we let 350 km² of lifeless desert define our exact statistical noise bar (2.73 dB HH, 2.03 dB HV).
  • Breaking the "Purple Radar" Curse: Traditional HH / HV / HH-HV composites paint both windy lakes and dry dirt purple; our Decoupled Physical Composite gives plants, concrete cities, calm/windy water, and bare soil distinct, intuitive colors.
  • Saving a Forgotten Island with Pure Radar Physics: Standard hole-filling flooded +43 m-tall El-Qarn Island inside Lake Qarun (100% false water); stacking 9 interferometric coherence maps and wave-roughness checks cut false island water down to 0.80% using radar alone.
  • A Storyteller That Refuses to Hallucinate: Pairing a 6-chapter guided tour and Echo AI with hard scientific truth labels (Observation vs. Change vs. Hypothesis), plus a compressed client-side cube so live pixel clicks work even without a backend server.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

  • Strict Scientific Honesty: Keeping linear-power math separate from decibels, masking low-signal desert dunes near the -24.5 dB sensor noise floor, treating wind waves as a confounder rather than land change, and refusing to overclaim subsidence from 12-day atmospheric phase noise.
  • Version & Geometry Consistency: Never mixing early BETA granules with calibrated PROVISIONAL (CRID P05023) passes, and locking every comparison to identical Track 129, Frame 016, and Ascending orbit geometry so viewing angles never masquerade as physical change.
  • No Fabricated Data & Independent Cross-Checks: Zero simulated pixels in the product, strict separation between primary NISAR measurements and external optical/weather context, explicit Pass 10 temporal holdout backtesting (seed = 42), and strict error reporting if an Echo AI key is missing.
  • Human-Centered Accessibility & Bandwidth: Progressive disclosure (5 clean tabs, plain-English readouts, minimizable legends, and downloadable COGs) paired with 30× cloud payload compression (255.6 MB → 9.46 MB) so anyone—on any connection—can explore the story in under 3 minutes.
